chapters.title: Why you're still in it
chapters.teaser: The real reason your soul keeps saying 'let's see where it goes'.

chapters.title: What you actually want
chapters.teaser: Not what sounds chill. What you'd ask for if you weren't worried.

chapters.title: How you read mixed signals
chapters.teaser: Your decoding habit, and a better way to get information.

chapters.title: The talk, your way
chapters.teaser: How to ask 'what are we' in words that fit your soul.

chapters.title: Your line
chapters.teaser: The one thing you shouldn't keep accepting.

chapters.title: Either way, you're okay
chapters.teaser: What comes next, whatever answer you get.

text.why-you-stay: Gye Water is the rain, intuitive and gentle. You feel deeply and quietly, and a situationship lets you keep those feelings unspoken, which can feel safe. You might stay because you sense something real between you, a connection that doesn't need words. Or because asking would feel far too exposing. Ask yourself softly: is the mystery here romantic, or is it just unclear? Romantic mystery makes you feel more alive. Unclear makes you feel more anxious. You can tell the difference if you're honest. Put your hand on your chest, ask the question, and notice what comes up first.
text.what-you-want: You want emotional closeness, to be understood without having to explain every single thing. Gye Water hopes that other people will simply intuit what it needs. They won't, not fully, not even the kind ones. So write your want down plainly: I want to know where I stand. I want to feel safe. I want us to be a real thing with a name. Seeing it in words makes it real, and it makes it much easier to say out loud when the moment comes. Read it back to yourself a few times until it stops sounding scary and starts sounding simply true.
text.mixed-signals: When signals are mixed, you absorb them. Their mood quietly becomes your mood. Gye Water can go from happy to anxious on the strength of one short reply. Your intuition is a real and useful tool, but in fog everything looks bigger and closer than it is. Try writing down facts only: when they reached out, what they did, what they actually said. Leave out the guesses about what it meant. Fog clears remarkably fast once it's on paper. Read the list the next morning, in daylight, when everything feels a little more manageable.
text.the-talk: Your talk can be soft, but it has to contain actual words. Gye Water tends to hint and hope. Try a direct, gentle sentence: I've been feeling more for you, and I'd like to know where we are. You could write it down first to find the right phrasing. Then say it rather than text it, if you can, so your voice carries what the words can't. They deserve to hear the real you, and you deserve to see their face when they answer. If your voice shakes, let it. Shaking and honest is far better than steady and hidden.
text.your-line: Your line is emotional uncertainty that leaves you drained. If you're more anxious than happy, more confused than close, more alone than together, that is your line. Decide what you need to feel steady, and when it's missing, step back gently. You don't need a big confrontation or a dramatic exit. Rain simply moves on when the season changes, and nobody accuses the rain of being unfair. You're allowed to change seasons too. Write your line in your journal on a calm, clear day, so you can read it back when the fog rolls in. Then trust the version of you who wrote it.
text.either-way: Either way, you'll be okay, and you'll be clearer than you are right now. If they want more, keep using your words, every week, even when it feels exposing. If not, let yourself feel it fully, cry if you need to, and then let it pass through. You deserve someone who wants to understand you, and who finally gets the chance to, because you spoke up instead of waiting to be guessed. That's a win, whatever their answer was. Then go and stand in actual rain for a minute. It helps more than it should.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You feel so much, Gye, even when you don't say it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Exactly. You don't say it. They're not mind readers.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Writing your feelings down first is a great idea.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Then say them out loud. Hints are not a language.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Facts on paper clear the fog.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: One reply shouldn't control your whole mood. Phone down.

spring.intro: Spring Gye is soft rain that helps things grow. Wood ruled your birth season and Water feeds Wood, so your care is quiet, attentive and generous. In a situationship you're probably the one who listens, remembers and checks in. Your attention helps them bloom, and you hope it'll make them notice what's right in front of them. Spring Gye's trap is giving softly and waiting to be seen. They might not see it, not because you aren't worth it but because rain is easy to take for granted. Say what you want in words. Hints are lovely. Words are clear.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Hints are lovely. They have also not worked for four months, Gye.

summer.intro: A summer cloud has a lot of heat to cool. Fire ruled your season, Gye, and Water controls Fire, so you're constantly soothing, smoothing, keeping things pleasant. In a situationship you might be absorbing all the heat: their unpredictability, their busy weeks, their vague plans. You make it easy for them and hard for yourself. Summer Gye can evaporate, slowly losing yourself in their weather. Notice whether you feel more yourself or less since this started. If less, it's time to ask for something solid. A plan. A label. A sign they're bringing some shade too.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Do you feel more like yourself since this started, or less? Be honest, Gye.

autumn.intro: Autumn Gye is mist rising off cold stone, well fed by Metal, which ruled your birth season. Metal generates Water, so your intuition is sharp and usually right. You already sense what this situationship is and isn't. The issue isn't reading the signals. It's trusting them. Autumn Gye can second-guess a clear read because the hopeful version is so vivid. Write down what you actually feel about where this is heading, then compare it with what they've actually done. Your gut has been taking notes. Let it speak when you have the talk.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your gut figured this out weeks ago. Your hope is filibustering, Gye.

winter.intro: Winter Gye is snow, quiet and complete. Water ruled your season and doubled your element, so your imagination runs rich and your feelings run deep. In a situationship you can build an entire relationship in your head: future trips, inside jokes, how you'd introduce them. The real one is thinner. Winter Gye's blind spot is preferring the imagined version because it never disappoints. But it also never holds you. Bring one daydream into the real world. Suggest one of those plans. Their response, in actual life, is the clarity you've been looking for.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Take one daydream and actually suggest it, Gye. Real life is warmer.

strength.strong: Your chart feeds your rain generously, Gye, so your intuition and imagination run strong. In a situationship you might feel very sure you know what they feel, often before they've said it. That certainty can push you to act on your version of them. The blind spot is that intuition fills the gaps with your own colours. Ask instead of assuming. What they actually say may surprise you, in either direction. Clear words beat even the best reading, and you deserve to hear theirs.
strength.weak: With little support for your Day Master, Gye, you can disappear into a stronger personality's weather. In a situationship you might be quiet about your needs, gentle about their lapses, endlessly understanding. The blind spot is being so easy to be with that you become easy to overlook. Your softness is lovely. It also needs a voice. Say one clear thing you want this week. If it lands, good. If it doesn't, that tells you something important too, and you can act on it.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and definition. In a situationship you might rush clarity, or picture a whole future before the other person has caught up to the present. Your drive is a good thing. Just give them room to answer at their own pace once you've asked. Ask once, clearly, then step back and let the answer come. Balance with a little Metal: clear boundaries, finished business, knowing when something needs pruning rather than more growth.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means starting things, including the talk, feels hard. You might let an undefined situation drift on and on simply because initiating anything feels heavy. Build momentum in small steps: decide what you want, write it down, choose a day to ask. Spend time outdoors and around green things. You don't need to grow everything at once. You only need one honest question, asked once, out loud.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire means big feelings, fast. In a situationship you might swing between excitement and frustration in the same evening, and want answers right now. Slow your pace a little. Pick a calm moment for the talk, not a heated one. Cool down with water: rest, quiet nights in, a walk before sending any big message. Your passion is attractive. Just don't let it make your decisions at midnight.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means expressing feelings and being seen can feel hard. You might keep this situationship low-key so that nobody, including you, has to admit it matters. Turn the light up a little. Let your feelings show in small ways. Be visible in your own life too: plans, friends, sunlight, music. The more you shine for yourself, the easier the honest question becomes when you finally ask it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you wait, stay steady, and stay put, sometimes for too long. In a situationship you may tolerate a lack of definition because change feels disruptive and messy. Bring in a bit of movement: pick a day by which you'll have the talk, and keep it. Let some Wood in, growth and fresh starts. Stable doesn't have to mean stuck, and patient doesn't have to mean silent.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means stability is hard to find, and an undefined relationship can make you feel even more unsteady than usual. Ground yourself first: routines, regular meals, a dependable circle of friends. Then have the talk from a steady place, not a shaky one. You'll think more clearly and ask more clearly when your own ground is solid under your feet, whatever the answer turns out to be.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal means you want clarity and might cut too fast to get it. In a situationship you may issue ultimatums or go cold the moment things feel vague. Your boundaries are strong, which is good. Soften the delivery: ask with curiosity first, decide second. Water helps here: rest, reflection, letting a feeling be felt before you act on it.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard. In a situationship you may accept less than you want and keep telling yourself it's fine. Practise clear edges: decide your line and write it down somewhere you'll see it. Say no to plans that don't work for you. White and silver, decluttering, finishing things all support you. A boundary isn't harsh. It's honesty about what you need.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means overthinking and very deep feeling. In a situationship you might analyse every message and drown in what-ifs that never happen. Your intuition is valuable, but it needs a shore to land on. Earth helps: routines, physical activity, friends who ground you. Put a limit on the analysis. Ask the question instead of guessing the answer.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means reflection and rest get skipped. You might keep the situationship busy and fun so you never have to stop and think about what it actually is. Make space for quiet: a journal, a slow evening, a moment alone to ask yourself what you really want here. Clarity starts inside you before it's ever spoken to them, and it's worth the quiet.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you've planned your future together. They haven't planned Saturday.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy is lovely. Point it at what you want, not only at them.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: one great date and you're naming the dog. Breathe.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is magnetic. Let them match it before you double it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: you've waited so patiently you've basically become their furniture.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is a gift. It's fair to ask for steadiness back.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal: you've drafted an ultimatum. Maybe try a question first.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is strength. Soften the delivery and it lands beautifully.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you analysed one 'haha' with three friends and a tarot app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your sensitivity notices so much. Check the signals against actual actions too.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make it hard to picture what you want. Try imagining it.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no vision. You're seeing where it goes without looking anywhere.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make it hard to show interest. A little warmth helps.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. They genuinely cannot tell if you like them. Neither can I.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it easy to drift. Choose one thing you're sure about.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no ground. You change your mind about them every other day.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal can blur your line. You can decide what you won't accept.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means no line. You'll accept 'wyd' at midnight forever.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make feelings hard to say. Try writing them first.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. You'd rather move countries than say 'I like you.'

gap-wood.title: The moon screenshot and 'thursday 7?'
gap-wood.text: A Gap Wood gives you shelter. Their certainty is restful. When you're spiralling about something small at 11 p.m., Gap says one sensible sentence and suddenly the room is quieter. You send songs; they send logistics. You send the moon; they send 'nice. thursday 7?'. There's something sweet in that, and something lonely. The drift in this pair tends to come from your side going quiet. You hint at what you want with a playlist, a story about a friend who just got engaged, a carefully casual 'what are we even doing haha'. Gap reads the words literally and moves on. Meanwhile you may be quietly absorbing Gap's stress, holding their bad days, and not mentioning that you'd like a little more holding back. Your signal is softness, and a tree can mistake soft for fine. For the talk, give Gap the version without the mist. It can be short: I like you a lot. I want us to be together, with an actual word for it. Do you want that too? Write it down first if that helps. You are allowed to say the thing directly. Gap tends to answer direct things directly.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, the moon screenshot is beautiful. Add a sentence under it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap, 'nice, thursday 7?' is not how you answer the moon.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Answer the feeling first, then the logistics.

eul-wood.title: The exhibition that has been 'soon' since July
eul-wood.text: An Eul Wood is the gentlest kind of sunshine for you. They're social without being loud, warm without being pushy, and they make your quiet feel welcome. You share songs. You have a joke about the moon. You've talked through four hours of a night without noticing. It's tender, and it's very undefined. The drift comes from both of you avoiding the uncomfortable part. When your mood goes grey, you withdraw, and Eul tends to try to cheer you up. If the cheering doesn't work, Eul can quietly feel rejected, and you won't know because neither of you says it. Plans float: the exhibition, the weekend away, the dinner with Eul's friends. 'Soon' becomes the most used word in your chat. Your signal is silence, which you mean as needing time and Eul may read as distance. For the talk, you don't have to be loud. You just have to be clear for one sentence. Write it first if that helps: I like you so much. I want us to be a couple, with a name for it. Would you like that too? Then send the song, if you like. But send the sentence first.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Shared playlist, 3 a.m. talks. You two are a soft little film.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: That exhibition has been 'soon' since July. Pick a date.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sentence first, song second.

byeong-fire.title: Rainbow weather and the badly timed joke
byeong-fire.text: A Byeong Fire is bright, warm and loud, and somehow they make your rainy days feel less heavy. You love how easily they talk to strangers. You love how they make plans out of nothing. You also, sometimes, feel a bit drowned out. The drift here is weather. When you're low, you go quiet. Byeong tends to read quiet as disinterest and either pushes harder or jokes to lighten the mood. To Byeong, the joke is kindness. To you, it can feel like being dismissed. So you withdraw further, and the sky gets stormy. Byeong's messages arrive in floods, voice notes and emojis; yours come slowly, carefully, sometimes not at all. From Byeong's side, slow replies can look like fading interest. Your signal is quiet, and to a sun, quiet looks like cloud cover. For the talk, you don't need to be loud. You need one clear sentence and maybe a heart emoji afterwards so Byeong knows you're still there: I'm quieter than you, but I'm really into you. I want this to be real. Do you? And tell Byeong, kindly, that when you share something soft, you'd like them to sit with it before they joke.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sunshine and drizzle. This is rainbow weather.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, no jokes for two minutes. You can do it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, one heart emoji says 'still here'. Send it.

jeong-fire.title: Waiting in the rain for a knock
jeong-fire.text: A Jeong Fire feels everything as deeply as you do, which is rare and slightly overwhelming. They see your moods, they remember the song you mentioned once, they write messages that make you cry a little on the bus. And they need clarity in a way that sometimes makes you want to disappear into fog. The drift here is between your silence and their need to know. When you're low, you withdraw. That's how you look after yourself. Jeong can read the withdrawal as rejection and reach for reassurance, asking what's wrong, what this is, where you went. You feel those questions as pressure and drift further, and then both of you go quiet and stay quiet. Long silences become the shape of the situationship. Your signal is mystery, and to an anxious flame, mystery looks like a threat. For the talk, you don't have to give everything. Give one clear sentence: I go quiet sometimes, and it isn't about you. I'd like us to be a real couple. Would you? Then agree, together, that going quiet is fine and never a punishment. A candle can live with rain. It needs to know it's still wanted.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Two very soft hearts. Gentle with each other, please.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Silence is allowed. Silence as punishment is not.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, one clear sentence. Jeong, one deep breath.

mu-earth.title: Mist, a poem and 'bring an umbrella'
mu-earth.text: 戊癸 is one of the five heavenly combinations, and with a Mu Earth, you feel it: mist settling on a mountain. Mu is calm, steady and kind in a practical way. They make you feel safe, and your moods seem to bother them less than they bother most people. The drift here is that you speak in feelings and Mu speaks in facts. You send a poetic message about the rain and how it reminds you of them. Mu replies 'yes, bring an umbrella tomorrow'. You can feel unseen. Mu genuinely meant it as love. When you share a worry about where this is going, Mu might offer a plan instead of comfort. Your moods also shift more than Mu is used to, and Mu might read that as changeability. Your signal is subtle and poetic, and a mountain tends to read only the literal layer. For the talk, appreciate Mu's steadiness for what it is, and then say the thing without the poem: I'd like us to be together, properly. I need you to tell me how you feel, not just what to do. Can you do that for me? Mu responds best to plain requests. Give one.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: 戊癸, mist on the mountain. Gentle and rare.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, 'bring an umbrella' is not a reply to a poem.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, say it without the poem once.

gi-earth.title: 'What's wrong?' 'Nothing.'
gi-earth.text: A Gi Earth is the garden bed that catches your rain. They're caring, attentive and steady, and with them your moods feel less dangerous. They notice when you're low. They want to help. Sometimes they want to help a bit too much. The drift here is the 'what's wrong?' 'nothing' loop. You feel something shift, you go quiet. Gi asks what's wrong. You say nothing, because you don't know yet, or because saying it feels too much. Gi tries to organise the mood, suggests a walk, a plan, a solution. You feel managed. Gi starts tidying the kitchen. You start drifting, and the evening passes with neither of you saying the real thing. The question of what this is lives in that same murk. Your signal is withdrawal, which Gi reads as a problem to fix. For the talk, try to answer Gi's actual question, even with something partial: I'm not sure what I'm feeling yet, but I know I want to be with you. Shall we make it official? Gi does better with half an answer than with 'nothing'. Give the half.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Rain on the garden. Gentle, if nobody fights over the mud.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: 'What's wrong?' 'Nothing.' The longest evening in history.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, give half an answer. Gi, give some space.

gyeong-metal.title: The fog photo with no caption
gyeong-metal.text: A Gyeong Metal is tough love with a soft centre, and somehow you're the one who gets to see the centre. With you, Gyeong is protective and almost gentle. They send one-line messages like orders of the day, 'eat something', 'take a jacket', and you find it oddly romantic. The drift here is pace and pressure. Gyeong wants clear answers, ideally right now. You need a day to know what you even feel. When Gyeong asks what this is, you tend to go quiet or send something poetic instead, and Gyeong gets frustrated and blunter. Their bluntness hurts you more than they realise, and you withdraw. You might even keep small things to yourself to avoid their reaction. That looks like secrecy to Gyeong, and it makes them push harder. Your signal is mist, which steel can read as hiding. For the talk, tell Gyeong upfront that you need time, and set your own small deadline: I care about you a lot. Let me think about this properly, and let me answer you tomorrow. Then answer. Plainly, the actual question. Gyeong can handle almost anything except not knowing.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The sword and the morning dew. Tough love, soft centre.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, ask what the fog photo means. It means something.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, ask for a day. Then come back with the answer.

sin-metal.title: Small comment, long silence
sin-metal.text: A Sin Metal shines quietly in your rain. They're precise, refined, and much softer underneath than they let most people see. With you, they're gentle. You notice things about them nobody else does, and they seem to love that. The drift here has a pattern. Sin makes a small, sharp comment, often about something minor. You go quiet because it stung. Sin reads your quiet as coldness and goes quiet too. Neither of you says anything, and after a week all that's left is the distance. Your moods can confuse Sin, who likes to understand things clearly. Sin's critiques can sting you, even when they're small. You both overthink texts, you both take your time, and the 'what are we' question gets lost in all the careful silences. Your signal is withdrawal, which Sin can read as rejection. For the talk, say the sting out loud, gently: that comment hurt a bit, and I went quiet. Then say the bigger thing: I'd like to be your partner, properly. Would you want that? Sin responds well to clear and kind. And make a pact: slow replies are just slow, never a message.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Silver in the rain. Delicate and quietly beautiful.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Small comment, long silence. You two invented this.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Name the sting out loud. Then name what you want.

im-water.title: Talked over at the party, noticed by the rain
im-water.text: An Im Water is the ocean, and you're the rain. Same element, very different scale. Im is big, restless, brilliant, and they make your world feel wider. You make theirs feel deeper, even if they don't always say so. The drift here is that you can feel overshadowed. In a group, Im takes up the room and sometimes talks over you without noticing. You notice. You store it. Im's restlessness can feel overwhelming, and when Im disappears into a new obsession, you go quiet too. Both of you avoid conflict by drifting, so long gaps open up where neither of you says what's wrong. Your poetic messages and Im's bursts pass each other like boats at night. The 'what are we' question sits unasked. Your signal is quietness, which Im can easily miss in all the noise. For the talk, ask Im for something small and specific: a quiet evening, just you two. Then say it: I like you so much. I'd like us to be a real couple, not a maybe. How do you feel? And mention, kindly, the times you felt talked over. Im may not have noticed, and that's exactly why it's worth saying.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The ocean and the rain. Same water, different depths.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, you talked over Gye at the party. Gye noticed.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Silence isn't rejection. Say so, both of you.

gye-water.title: Two raindrops, one window, no plan
gye-water.text: Two Gye Waters in a situationship are two raindrops on one window: tender, dreamy, a bit lost. You send each other song links, poems, half-finished thoughts at midnight. You understand each other's silences. With each other, you don't have to explain why you're sad on a Tuesday. It's one of the gentlest connections there is. The drift for two raindrops is that nobody decides. Plans stay vague, 'maybe this weekend', 'we'll see', and practical things like holidays or meeting friends float away. When either of you is hurt, you withdraw, and the other often withdraws too, to give space. Then two quiet people are waiting for each other in the rain. Moods amplify: when you're both low, a rainy week can turn into a rainy month, and nobody pulls the other out. You might also keep small secrets to avoid upsetting each other, and that slowly builds distance. Your signal is softness, which the other reads with perfect understanding and no next step. For the talk, someone has to be the one who says it plainly. Write it first if you need to: I want us to be together. Not maybe. Really. Do you? And agree that a missed reply is never a test.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Two raindrops on one window. So gentle together.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: 'Maybe this weekend' is not a plan. It's weather.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say it plainly. Not maybe. Really.
